app.name: Times Tables
app.tagline: A few calm minutes a day.

common.offline: Offline — your progress is saved on this phone
common.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
common.updateReady: A new version is ready. Tap to update.

welcome.title: Welcome!
welcome.body: Ask your parent for a 6-digit code to link this phone.
welcome.invalidCode: That code didn't work. Codes last 15 minutes — ask for a new one.
welcome.tooMany: Too many tries. Please wait a few minutes.

home.startCheckup: Let's see what you already know
home.startCheckupNote: No wrong answers here — just a quick look.
home.bonusLocked: Bonus rows ×11 and ×12 unlock when your map is nearly all green.

practice.newFactNote: Here's a way to work it out. Then I'll ask you.
practice.revealNote: Here's a way to remember it. It'll come back in a moment.
practice.checkupIntro: Answer what you can. If you're not sure, tap “Not sure yet” — that's useful too.
practice.breakBody: Keep going, or finish the rest another day.

parent.title: Parent area

errors.email_taken: An account with that email already exists.
errors.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Please wait a few minutes.

parent.name: First name or nickname
parent.noChildren: Add your first child to get started.
parent.linkSteps: On your child's phone, open {url} in Chrome and enter this code:
parent.linkInstall: Then tap ⋮ → “Add to Home screen” so it opens like an app.
parent.readAloudNote: Questions and steps are read out with the phone's own voice. If the phone has no voice installed, nothing is read and everything still works.
parent.paceNote: Measured against how fast your child types on their phone.
parent.missingNote: Like ? × 7 = 56, a first step into division. They start once facts are fluent, and don't change the fact map.

ten.summary: Times 10: {n} moves up one place and a 0 fills the gap, making {p}.

nine.less: The answer starts with {tens}, one less than {n}.
nine.sum: And its digits add up to 9: {tens} + {ones} = 9.

lesson.groups_1: Here is a plate of apples. How many apples are on it?
lesson.groups_2: Here is another plate, with {each} more. How many now?
lesson.groups_3: One more plate of {each}. How many now?
lesson.groups_4: {n} plates, with {each} on each one: that's {n} groups of {each}. We write it {n} × {each}.
lesson.groups_5: Your turn: {n} plates, with {each} on each. How many apples?
lesson.arrays_1: Here is a row of squares. How many are there?
lesson.arrays_2: Now two rows of {cols}. How many?
lesson.arrays_3: Three rows of {cols}. How many now?
lesson.arrays_5: Turn it around: now it's {rows} rows of {cols}. Same squares!
lesson.skip_first: Let's count in {n}s. Jump {n} from 0. Where do you land?
lesson.countAgain: Not quite. Count them again. You can do it!
lesson.doneNote: You worked out every step of “{title}”.

games.title: Games
games.pairsHow: Tap a sum, then its answer.
games.rowPick: Pick a row of your map to fill in.
games.rowPattern: Look: each answer is {n} more than the one before.

turnaround.summary: {a} rows of {b} turned around is {b} rows of {a}: both make {p}.
turnaround.intro: You have seen this fact the other way around.
